after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le z\le 2{x}^{2},\,0\le y\le 2xz}.
$$
after.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2xz}2x\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2xz}2x\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{2xz}2x\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}2x[y]_{y=0}^{y=2xz}dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}2x(2xz)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}4{x}^{2}z\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}4{x}^{2}z\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2{x}^{2}}4{x}^{2}z\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}[{z}^{2}]_{z={x}^{2}}^{z=2{x}^{2}}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}((2{x}^{2})^{2}-({x}^{2})^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{6}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{6}\,dx & ={[\frac{6{x}^{7}}{7}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{6}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{8}z\,dy]dA
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 4}.
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}z\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}z[y]_{y={x}^{3}}^{y=8}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(8-{x}^{3})[{\int }_{0}^{4}z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(8-{x}^{3}){[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=4}\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{[8x-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =8(16-4) \\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{8}z\,dy]dA
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 4}.
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}z\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}z[y]_{y={x}^{3}}^{y=8}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(8-{x}^{3})[{\int }_{0}^{4}z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(8-{x}^{3}){[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=4}\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{[8x-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =8(16-4) \\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}6y\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,x\le y\le 1-z},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis,  and the curve $z=1-x$ in the first quadrant.
after.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}6y\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{1-z}6y\,dy]dA.
$$

 

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{1-z}6y\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}3[{y}^{2}]_{y=x}^{y=1-z}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}3((1-z)^{2}-{x}^{2})\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

 

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070114/assets/819b5b00967bf485068c146602bf962481b21b75d5319113fd6bd94366e84be0.png)

 

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}3((1-z)^{2}-{x}^{2})\,dA & ={∬}_{D}3((1-z)^{2}-{x}^{2})\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}3((1-z)^{2}-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-(1-z)^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1-x}-3{x}^{2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=1-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-{x}^{3}+1-3{x}^{2}(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\,\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-{x}^{3}+x]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(\,\frac{1}{2}-1+1)-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

${∭}_{R}\frac{\pi x}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\,\text{d}V=$
after.worked_solution:
For a type III region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type III region enclosed between the back surface $y={u}_{1}(x,z)=0$ and the front surface $y={u}_{2}(x,z)=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070114/assets/63cffdee00edd80c4a0abdc30e8e45b1af29078b8bc4902bf3f60b7b4a104172.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,0\le y\le 2}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type II *plane* region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡z.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070114/assets/dc72aeb4b554d88f00083dc6bf6f8ca4244e1b7683c8dec10ba0491c678a5603.png)

Hence, $D={(x,z)\,:\,1\le z\le e,\,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡z}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{\pi x}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi x}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}x[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}x{[\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

${∭}_{R}\frac{\pi x}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\,\text{d}V=$
content.worked_solution:
For a type III region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type III region enclosed between the back surface $y={u}_{1}(x,z)=0$ and the front surface $y={u}_{2}(x,z)=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070114/assets/63cffdee00edd80c4a0abdc30e8e45b1af29078b8bc4902bf3f60b7b4a104172.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,0\le y\le 2}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type II *plane* region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡z.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070114/assets/dc72aeb4b554d88f00083dc6bf6f8ca4244e1b7683c8dec10ba0491c678a5603.png)

Hence, $D={(x,z)\,:\,1\le z\le e,\,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡z}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{\pi x}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi x}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}x[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}x{[\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi y}{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$
